sections.title: Study area: Franz Josef
sections.html:
Franz Josef Glacier, West Coast, New Zealand · Westland Tai Poutini National Park (RGI 7 G-18-01930). The picture box is 14.92 x 16.31 km (set by the owner); the 3D strip along the glacier is 6261 m long and 4460 m wide, 27.9 km² (computed from the saved strip).

Outlines drawn on the map: GLIMS Glacier Database · six dated outlines; dates 1600-09-09 (moraine mapping); 1978-01-01; 2000-04-13; 2009-02-17; 2016-03-11; 2019-03-28. Different analysts and methods: do not derive area change by mixing epochs without saying so. The 1600 record is moraine mapping, not an ice outline at a date.

sections.title: What was measured
sections.html:
One measured surface, not one per year. The 3D view of Franz Josef Glacier shows a single surface. Everywhere it is the seamless LINZ West Coast LiDAR 1 m DEM (heights NZVD2016 as delivered, a 4 m mosaic of the strip, CC-BY-4.0). On the glacier it is the newest lidar flight day for each cell, decoded here from the raw point clouds (OpenTopography, flights of 2022-04 to 2025-03), blended into the DEM over 150 m at the 1978 outline, with a light smoothing. Where the DEM has no data, Copernicus GLO-30 minus 5.8 m is used. The pictures of every year are draped on this same surface.

  • The flight days. Eleven flight days (UTC, from GPS time): 2022-04-13, 2022-04-18, 2022-04-19, 2023-01-27, 2024-01-07, 2024-04-20, 2024-05-22, 2024-05-23, 2024-12-16, 2025-02-26, 2025-03-12. The LINZ DEM over the glacier is a patchwork of these days; the catalogue gives no day for a pixel (computed here from 133 point-cloud tiles).
  • Where each day lies. The lower tongue was flown on 2024-05-23 (a few cells at the very front on 2024-01-07 and 2024-05-22); the central glacier on 2025-03-12; a diagonal band on 2025-02-26; the south-east upper part on 2024-04-20 over 2022-04-18/19. Latest flight day per ice cell (computed): 2025-03-12 53.2%, 2024-04-20 29.8%, 2025-02-26 8.7%, 2024-05-23 7.3%, 2022-04-19 1.0%. Flight days in the glacier surface: 2024-01-07 to 2025-03-12.
  • The best picture. 2025-02-14 is the picture closest in time to the flight days that make up the glacier surface: mean |image - flight day| 0.32 yr (2024: 0.75, 2026: 1.32, computed).
  • Not on the site. There is no surface for each year, no ice bed and no ice change for Franz Josef, and the functions that need several elevation models are switched off. A modelled surface for each year 2016 to 2026 was built as a local experiment and is not shown: its scale rests on a mass balance transferred from other glaciers (below).

sections.title: How far to trust it: checks, limits and caveats
sections.html:
What the lidar says. A surface measured on several days, not a series of the same glacier. Where two flights overlap (all in the upper glacier, 1600 to 2900 m), the later minus the earlier surface is small: 2022-04-19 to 2024-04-20 -0.33 m [-0.9, +0.2]; 2024-04-20 to 2025-03-12 +0.57 m [+0.4, +0.9]; 2024-12-16 to 2025-03-12 -0.22 m [-1.2, +0.2] (median [quartiles], computed). Same-day or near-same-day pairs agree to 0.00 to 0.03 m. No overlap exists on the tongue (it has one date), so the lidar gives no measured lowering of the tongue. In the upper glacier snow, ice flux and melt nearly cancel (interpretation, not tested), so these changes are not mass balance.

  • Blend. DEM minus the glacier composite, median -0.7 / -0.8 / 0.0 / 0.0 m in the 200-800 / 800-1400 / 1400-2000 / 2000-2600 m bands (computed).
  • Mass balance. WGMS holds no mass-balance rows for Franz Josef (computed from mass_balance.csv, release 2026-02-10). A balance transferred from Brewster and Rolleston (median) was computed for the local experiment; it is modelled, not a measurement, and its scale is unconstrained.
  • ICESat-2. No usable shots below 1200 m (none on the tongue); above 1200 m the per-date median difference against the 2025-03-12 lidar ranges from 1.91 to 9.74 m (13 dates, 2019-2026). It cannot constrain the scale of the transfer; the test is inconclusive, not a confirmation.
  • GLO-30. Stable terrain: median GLO-30 minus lidar +5.8 m, MAD 5.66 m; this offset is large and poorly known. The acquisition period of GLO-30 was found in secondary sources only (the Product Handbook v5.0 itself NOT READ).
  • ASTER. Too noisy to constrain the lowering to better than metres (stable-terrain spread MAD 7.7 / 12.5 / 26.2 m at the 10th / 50th / 90th percentile of scenes). The tongue clearly thinned by tens of metres since 2016 (agrees with GLO-30), but ASTER cannot give the glacier-wide scale.
  • Pictures and surface. Pictures of years before 2024 show a larger glacier than the surface under them: the surface is the one of 2024 to 2025.

Cautions of each source

  • GLIMS Glacier Database · six dated outlines. Different analysts and methods: do not derive area change by mixing epochs without saying so. The 1600 record is moraine mapping, not an ice outline at a date.
  • WGMS · Fluctuations of Glaciers, front variation (WGMS_ID 899). A length change, not a front position: the zero point of the series is not an outline. Use it to check the yearly front arcs, not to fit them.
  • WGMS · state (area, length) rows. Sparse and of mixed origin; no numbers go on the site before checking the file wording.
  • WGMS · geodetic change rows (Zemp 2019, Hugonnet 2021). Glacier-wide means: not the tongue only, not a surface. Never fitted.
  • WGMS · mass balance tables. Absence in this release is not proof that no measurement exists elsewhere.
  • LINZ · West Coast LiDAR 1 m DEM and DSM (2020-2024). The survey DAY over the glacier is NOT known: the collection has a four-year range and the block maps showing which flight covers the box are images. Needs the point-cloud GPS times or the flight-line map. A glacier surface moves: one dated epoch only.
  • LINZ · Canterbury LiDAR 1 m DEM and DSM (2020-2025). Survey day over the box NOT known; may be a different epoch from the West Coast flights: check where they overlap.
  • GNS Science · Alpine Fault "Franz LiDAR" 2010. Whether the 66 km² area includes the glacier is NOT verified (the extent shapefile was not opened). Flown in July: snow on the glacier.
  • LINZ · New Zealand 8 m DEM (contour-derived). Interpolated from topographic contours: a composite of old survey dates. Never a dated ice surface.
  • ICESat-2 · ATL06 land-ice heights. Never fitted. Quality flags, steep slope and water/shadow contamination to be checked per track.
  • ASTER · AST14DEM and stereo. Optical, snow-cover sensitive; co-register on stable terrain first.
  • Lorrey et al. 2022 · end-of-summer snowline (EOSS) record, Southern Alps. Snowline elevation per glacier, no mass balance values read.
  • Farinotti et al. 2019 · consensus ice thickness. A model, never a measurement.
  • Victoria University of Wellington · glacier time-lapse cameras. A source for the yearly front series behind WGMS rows? Not verified.

sections.html:

sections.title: Size page: how this glacier is shown
sections.html:
The Size page shows the outline of Franz Josef Glacier in Area view (2D), which you can drag onto a city.

  • Outline. The GLIMS polygon of 2019-03-28 (Carrivick et al.; db_area 30.9982 km² as stated in the file). The area shown is computed here from the polygon.
  • True size. The outline is only moved, never scaled or turned into another shape.
  • Area only. No ice volume is shown on the size page for this glacier (the volume view needs stated ice volumes). The span and the number of times the outline fits in a city are computed here.
